_comment: Global registry of priority landscapes the observatory intends to cover — spread across IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology realms (terrestrial, freshwater, marine, polar, transitional). Drives the news layer (GDELT per newsQuery) and, as field records are authored, the scrollytelling. hasFieldRecord=true means a Darwin Core Archive exists at public/dwca/<id>/. newsQuery is tuned for English-language environmental coverage.
_authority: The Place Manifest (cinematic-language/place-manifest.ts, ADR-001) is authoritative for which places exist and which carry an archive. This file is a NEWS-layer registry, not a place registry: it is a superset (aspirational landscapes with no archive) and, deliberately, not a subset (a place may exist in the manifest and have no meaningful news feed). hasFieldRecord must be kept consistent with public/dwca/<id>/ by hand until it is derived. V1.4: coral-triangle corrected false->true, its archive having existed since M9b. RESOLVED 2026-09-12 (was: KNOWN GAP): epr-vents was absent because adding it required an authored newsQuery and a deep-sea vent field has effectively no GDELT coverage. The news layer was RETIRED on 2026-09-11, so that objection no longer holds — this file no longer drives a news feed. epr-vents is now present with newsQuery: null and the reason recorded, carrying its archive and its cited IUCN GET binding (M3.7). 2026-09-11: BOREAL GAP CLOSED. The registry carried svalbard-barents (Arctic sea ice and tundra) and bialowieza (temperate lowland old-growth) but had no boreal forest entry at all — an omission at biome scale in a registry whose stated purpose is to be the aspirational superset. Added wood-buffalo-boreal. The entry is a NAMED PLACE with a protected-area anchor, matching this registry's register, rather than an entry called "boreal forest", which would be a biome abstraction. Wood Buffalo National Park is the largest boreal protected area in the world and sits in Canada, one of the two countries the source assessment names. LIMITATION, STATED: one entry cannot represent a biome that spans Russia and Canada, and the Siberian half is the larger one — a Siberian counterpart is a later editorial decision, not an oversight here. Registry only: no scene, no page, no archive. See .agents/decisions/2026-09-11-security-assessment-as-source.md.

iucn_get.name: Coastal river deltas
iucn_get.source: IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology v2.1, profile MFT1.1 — Keith, D.A., Ferrer-Paris, J.R., Nicholson, E. et al. (2022), Nature 610, 513-518, doi:10.1038/s41586-022-05318-4. Profile text: https://osf.io/4dcea/download sheet 'Short description', sha256 d8f19b91cac3bc974c94026a1f9805e6201afde41559e648f36c16419331e092
iucn_get.justification: Profile: "At the convergence of terrestrial, freshwater and marine realms, coastal river deltas are shaped by river inflows that deposit sediment and ocean tides and currents that disperse it. Gradients of salinity and submergence and dynamic substrates create shifting mosaics of CHANNELS, islands, floodplains, intertidal and subtidal mud plains and sand beds THAT MAY BE REGARDED AS EMBEDDED PATCHES OF OTHER FUNCTIONAL GROUPS." Distribution: "Continental margins of high rainfall catchments globally." The Sundarbans is the seaward Ganges-Brahmaputra delta and its tidal channel network is that mosaic. The profile's own closing clause is why this place needs two elements rather than one: MFT1.2 is the mangrove forest embedded in the MFT1.1 delta, and neither describes the place alone.
iucn_get.assigned_from: GET profile text, quoted in justification (not a lexical match)
iucn_get.contains: MFT1.2, the intertidal mangrove forest listed after it. MFT1.1 is the containing delta mosaic and is therefore the primary element.

iucn_get.name: Intertidal forests and shrublands
iucn_get.source: IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology v2.1, profile MFT1.2 — Keith, D.A., Ferrer-Paris, J.R., Nicholson, E. et al. (2022), Nature 610, 513-518, doi:10.1038/s41586-022-05318-4. Profile text: https://osf.io/4dcea/download sheet 'Short description', sha256 d8f19b91cac3bc974c94026a1f9805e6201afde41559e648f36c16419331e092
iucn_get.justification: Profile: "Mangroves create structurally complex and productive ecosystems in the intertidal zone of depositional coasts, around tropical and warm temperate regions." Distribution: "Tropical and warm temperate coastlines with good sediment supply." The Sundarbans is a tropical intertidal mangrove forest on a high-sediment delta coast.
iucn_get.assigned_from: GET profile text, quoted in justification (not a lexical match)
iucn_get.embedded_in: MFT1.1. This is not a peer of the element above it: the MFT1.1 profile states that a delta's mosaic of channels, islands and flats 'may be regarded as embedded patches of other functional groups', and this mangrove forest is one of those patches. The containing group is listed first.

iucn_get.name: Boreal and temperate high montane forests and woodlands
iucn_get.source: IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology v2.1, profile T2.1 — Keith, D.A., Ferrer-Paris, J.R., Nicholson, E. et al. (2022), Nature 610, 513-518, doi:10.1038/s41586-022-05318-4. Profile text: https://osf.io/4dcea/download sheet 'Short description', sha256 d8f19b91cac3bc974c94026a1f9805e6201afde41559e648f36c16419331e092
iucn_get.justification: The EFG NAME says 'high montane' but the PROFILE is broader and is the authority: "In boreal and mountainous cold, seasonally snow-prone climates, acid soils support structurally simple forests made up of needle-leaf conifer trees." Distribution: "Cool regions (boreal zone or mountains...) of the Northern Hemisphere." T2.1 is therefore the boreal needle-leaf forest group, and Wood Buffalo's lowland taiga binds to it. PARTIAL BIND, stated: the Peace-Athabasca Delta component is a freshwater wetland complex that this single field does not capture and which is left unbound.

landscapes.iucn_get_partial: EXAMINED, NOT BOUND (2026-09-12). The Peace-Athabasca Delta is one of the world's largest inland freshwater deltas and is a real second ecosystem here, but no GET profile sentence justifies a code for it. TF1.4 Seasonal floodplain marshes fits the PROCESS — "Seasonal flooding and drying regimes characterise high productivity floodplain marshes" — but its only distribution sentence reads "Seasonal tropics and subhumid temperate regions", which excludes a delta at 59 degrees N. MFT1.1 Coastal river deltas is explicitly COASTAL and the PAD lies far inland. TF1.6 peat bogs and TF1.7 fens are boreal but are peatlands, not a delta. The typology carries no inland-delta group. An honest gap beats a plausible code, so this stays a one-element array.

_iucn_get_note: IUCN GET binding is a HAND-AUTHORED CROSSWALK, cited per element (rulings 2026-09-12). `iucn_get` is an ARRAY: a place can genuinely be more than one Ecosystem Functional Group, and a single field silently drops the second one. EVERY element carries its own full citation and its own quoted profile justification — the array must never become a place to park a guess. ELEMENT ORDER IS MEANINGFUL AND IS NOT ALPHABETICAL OR CHRONOLOGICAL: the primary, CONTAINING group is listed FIRST and an EMBEDDED group second. A two-element array is not two equal claims. Sundarbans is [MFT1.1 Coastal river deltas, MFT1.2 Intertidal forests and shrublands] because the mangrove forest sits as a patch inside the delta mosaic, which the MFT1.1 profile says of itself. Where the relationship is recorded it is also written onto the elements, as `contains` and `embedded_in`, so it survives an element being read alone. The former string-overlap matcher in research/sos_pipeline/sources/iucn_get.py is DELETED, not disabled: two controlled vocabularies that share no terminology cannot be bridged by lexical similarity, and a near miss is worse than no match because a wrong efg code misdescribes a biome while looking authoritative. NULL IS NOT AN EMPTY ARRAY. `iucn_get: null` with a one-word `iucn_get_unbound` reason means NOT EXAMINED — 'unbuilt' is a registry-only placeholder with no scene, no archive and no visitor-facing surface, and binding it is post-gate work. An empty array would claim the place was examined and nothing fitted, which is a different and stronger claim. Where a place WAS examined and a second element was rejected, that is recorded in `iucn_get_partial` with the reasoning. realm and biome NAMES are null because they are absent from the source workbook; realm_code and biome_code are authoritative.
